page: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v6 is a Dlsv6-family virtual machine configured with 32 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, this instance features 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. The memory configuration provides 2.0 GB of RAM per core, positioning this server in the low-memory or compute-focused tier. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data shows strong performance in several key areas. The server achieves top 25% results in Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, as well as in image processing, text processing, and Passmark CPU physics tests. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also place in the top 25%. For language model tasks, the instance achieves top-tier performance in text generation using a small 135M model, while prompt processing and larger model inference remain in the average tier. Static web serving throughput is also in the top 25%.

The primary hardware tradeoff is the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, which limits the instance's suitability for memory-intensive databases or large-scale caching layers. Additionally, the lack of local storage requires reliance on external network-attached storage. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high-density 32-vCPU configuration with dedicated allocation and a 4.2 GHz clock speed offers a resource-dense option for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints, optimizing compute spend per core.

This instance is suited for compute-bound tasks such as web serving, multi-threaded decompression, image processing, and software compilation. It is also applicable for lightweight LLM text generation and general-purpose workloads that fit within the 64.0 GB memory limit.
